summary.text: A 66-year-old man with no past medical history had fever, dry cough and vomiting one week before the onset of GBS symptoms, and was admitted to neurology in September 2020 with bilateral peripheral facial palsy, acute proximally pronounced symmetrical tetraparesis and acute headache. Examination showed graded limb weakness, areflexia, and numbness and tingling of all four limbs.

Electroneuromyography showed reduced motor amplitude in all four limbs, absent F waves and normal sensory conduction, and acute motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy was diagnosed. Cerebrospinal fluid showed albuminocytologic dissociation with protein 1.38 g/L, the COVID-19 PCR was positive, and MRI with angio-sequences showed cerebral venous thrombosis of the left sigmoid sinus. Further laboratory, serologic, thrombophilia and autoimmune tests were negative or unremarkable.

He was started on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg three times per day for 10 days and received 5 sessions of plasma exchange with low molecular weight heparin at a curative dose, relayed by a vitamin K antagonist. Respiratory and neurological state improved considerably, upper extremity weakness resolved after the plasma exchange course, repeat muscle testing was better, and a new oropharyngeal PCR was negative.
